executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning November 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to generate alerts in the Americas region with both animal and potential human spillover concerns, representing a critical biosafety-level pathogen under active monitoring. The southern hemisphere influenza season onset in late April 2026 coincides with ongoing RSV and pertussis resurgences, creating compounded respiratory disease burden. Additional vector-borne threats including dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and mpox are simultaneously circulating across the Americas, with measles outbreaks threatening vaccination-gap populations.
bottomLine: Multiple concurrent epidemic threats across the Americas and Europe demand coordinated response, with H5N1 avian influenza representing the highest pandemic-potential risk requiring immediate prioritization.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Dual epidemiological alerts issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained transmission pressure
Animal reservoir activity with documented spillover risk to humans in Americas region
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential requiring heightened surveillance at animal-human interface
threats.action: Immediate enhancement of zoonotic surveillance at poultry-human interfaces; activate pandemic preparedness protocols; coordinate with FAO and OIE for regional containment; ensure rapid diagnostic capacity at BSL-3 facilities

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 suggesting elevated case counts or geographic spread
Ongoing hyperendemicity across tropical and subtropical Americas
Potential for serotype shifts increasing severe dengue risk
threats.action: Strengthen vector control programs; ensure hospital surge capacity for severe dengue; enhance cross-border case reporting and serotyping surveillance

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Dedicated epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active transmission
BSL-3 select agent with documented sustained human-to-human transmission in the region
Continued circulation following 2022-2024 outbreak wave suggesting endemic establishment
threats.action: Maintain vaccination campaigns targeting high-risk populations; enforce enhanced case investigation and contact tracing; ensure BSL-3 diagnostic capacity and clinician awareness

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV (Southern Hemisphere Season Onset)
threats.pathogen: Influenza A/B viruses; Respiratory Syncytial Virus
signals: Epidemiological alert issued April 27 2026 marking start of southern hemisphere season
Prior alert January 2026 flagged simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation creating dual respiratory burden
Seasonal transition period historically associated with healthcare system strain
threats.action: Accelerate influenza vaccination uptake in southern hemisphere countries; prepare hospital surge capacity for pediatric RSV cases; monitor for antigenic mismatch between circulating strains and vaccine composition

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained or worsening trend
Resurgence pattern consistent with waning vaccine immunity and potential acellular vaccine effectiveness gaps
Multi-country alert scope suggests regional epidemic wave underway
threats.action: Boost vaccination coverage particularly in infants and pregnant women; investigate potential vaccine-strain mismatch; strengthen neonatal protection through maternal immunization programs

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating active transmission risk
BSL-3 pathogen with high case fatality rate in unvaccinated populations
Epizootic activity in non-human primates often precedes human spillover in Americas
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations; investigate epizootic primate die-offs as early warning signal; ensure yellow fever vaccine supply chains are functional in endemic zones

threats.name: Measles
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026 indicating active cases or outbreak clusters
Immunity gaps from COVID-19 pandemic disruption of routine immunization persist
Americas elimination status at risk if transmission chains are not rapidly interrupted
threats.action: Conduct emergency supplemental immunization activities in identified low-coverage areas; implement rapid outbreak response within 72 hours of confirmed cases; strengthen airport and border health screening

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: Epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026 indicating active transmission
Expanding Aedes vector habitat due to climate-driven range shifts increases exposure risk
No approved therapeutic treatment; burden falls on clinical management and vector control
threats.action: Intensify Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus vector surveillance and control; enhance clinical diagnostic capacity to distinguish from dengue; monitor for neurological complications in vulnerable populations

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are under active surveillance in this reporting period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) triggered dual PAHO alerts (November 2025 and March 2026) and represents the highest pandemic-potential biological threat in the dataset, with confirmed animal sector activity and human spillover risk across the Americas. Monkeypox virus (MPXV), also a BSL-3 select agent, remains in active circulation with a dedicated April 2026 PAHO update confirming ongoing transmission in the Americas. Yellow fever virus, a BSL-3 pathogen, received a March 2026 alert. All three pathogens require BSL-3 handling for diagnostic and research activities and warrant heightened biosecurity protocols at regional reference laboratories.
amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals identified in current report titles; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance surveillance should be prioritized given the multi-wave pertussis resurgence across the Americas

GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (February 2026) may signal broader antimicrobial or pharmaceutical misuse patterns requiring pharmacovigilance integration into health security frameworks
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen alert burden on Americas health systems suggests cumulative healthcare capacity stress risk entering mid-2026
Southern hemisphere influenza season onset in late April 2026 overlapping with active dengue and chikungunya transmission creates diagnostic confusion risk for febrile illness triage
Dual H5N1 alerts across a four-month span indicate persistent enzootic pressure rather than isolated events, elevating pandemic preparedness urgency
Resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases (pertussis, measles) across the Americas signal post-pandemic immunization coverage deficits not yet fully recovered
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports through April-May 2026 suggests sustained elevated threat environment in Europe concurrent with Americas burden
